info.text:
# Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity

## Before you start: the starter save

Start the Archipelago client and connect to your slot **before** booting the game. For a new seed the client
installs a **starter save** in your emulator (your old save is backed up in `%USERPROFILE%/AoC_Archipelago/
backups`). Then boot Age of Calamity in Ryujinx or Eden and pick **Continue**: the game's forced opening (The Battle
of Hyrule Field with Link and Impa) is skipped and you start on the world map with your starting heroes and the
seed's first missions (`first_mission`, default any story mission; with the default `mission_unlocks: items` you
start with 2 unlocked).

**The Battle of Hyrule Field** is a normal story mission: it can be in any slot,
has its own unlock item and real checks, and plays as the game's own first mission (the opening, then the battle as
Link) when you get to it. The client's game mod stops the game from forcing it at the start; the client installs the
mod by itself while the emulator is closed. (In Challenges Only it comes cleared in the starter save.)

**Switching seeds:** each save belongs to the seed it was played with. Connect to another seed with the game closed
and the client swaps the saves: the current one is kept in `%USERPROFILE%/AoC_Archipelago/saves`, and the other
seed gets its own save back (or a starter save if it's new). While the game runs another seed's save, the client
leaves the game alone until you close it. A save with progress the client has never seen with any seed is only
replaced by `/starter_save` (it's kept as "unclaimed"). `/saves` lists which save belongs to which seed.

**Switching emulators:** one seed's save can live in both Ryujinx and Eden. Start the game once in the other
emulator, close it, and type `/sync_saves`; the client then keeps both copies the same whenever no game runs. Open
only one emulator at a time.

## Where is the options page?

The [player options page for this game](../player-options) contains all the options you need to configure and export a
config file.

## What does randomization do to this game?

Heroes, upgrades, quest rewards, weapons and filler are shuffled into the multiworld; the things you accomplish become
checks that send items to other players.

**Checks (locations)** - story mission clears always; optionally (the `weapon_checks`, `challenge_checks` and
`quest_checks` toggles, default challenges and quests): weapon pickups, challenge missions and side quests.
`difficulty_checks` adds one check per mission (and challenge) for each harder difficulty you clear it on. When
there are more items than checks, story and challenge clears get bonus checks (sent with the clear).
`side_check_density` thins the quest, challenge and Korok checks for shorter games. Quests for services open from
the start (stables, shops, dye shop, Sheikah Sensor, the Expansion Pass's Royal Ancient Lab; options in the "Open from the Start" group) hold no check. Expansion Pass
content (on by default with `include_dlc`) is treated like the base game's: the 8 Guardian of Remembrance missions
are story missions (goal, unlock items), EX challenges and quests are checks, and the DLC heroes are items. Without
the DLC in your emulator the client warns you, and `/no_dlc` takes it out of the goal and sends its checks.

**Items**
- Heroes: you start with `starting_character_count` (default 4) random heroes from `starting_character_pool`;
  the rest arrive as items. `hint_heroes` hints them all from the start.
- Mission unlocks (`mission_unlocks: items`): each story mission opens with its own item; `hint_mission_unlocks`
  hints them all.
- Upgrades: Heart Containers, Combo Upgrades, Special Gauge Upgrades and Enhanced Abilities per hero, plus
  Progressive Weapon Capacity, Progressive Seal Slot and Weapon Fusion.
- Quest rewards (`quest_reward_items`, 0 = vanilla). Rewards that only raise a number (hearts, lessons, apple
  capacity...) are progressive items; groups of different rewards (recipes, shops, stables, discounts, Smithy
  upgrades, research quests, dyes, Divine Beast upgrades, EX reward quests) are one item per reward, named after
  its quest, such as `Recipe (A Feast of Greens)`. Most give their reward directly: recipes, the
  Sheikah Sensor and its research, Divine Beast upgrades, rune cooldowns, heart recovery, damage taken, enemy XP, treasure detector,
  blacksmith and rust/seal upgrades, discounts, Smithy upgrades, Training Camp and cooking lessons, dyes, apple
  capacity, research rewards, Expansion Pass abilities and royal gift weapons. The client undoes a quest's own reward until its item arrives. Maz Koshia's trials are the exception: each trial is the next fight, so its item opens the quest.
- Royal Ancient Lab rewards (with `lab_checks`): each node you buy sends a check; its reward is an item, such as `Buy Apples (An Abundance of Apples)` or a lab weapon. All 35 nodes are open from the start; each still needs its materials and its own condition, such as defeating 100 enemies with Remote Bombs.
- Weapons.
- Filler (weights set by `filler_weights`): character XP gifts, free weapons (Extra Weapon 1, Weapon Bundle 3, Large
  Weapon Bundle 5, for different heroes), Rupee Pouches, Small / regular / Large Material Bundles, Hearty Meals.

## Goal

`goal_story_missions` (2-28, default 20; the base game has 20, the DLC adds 8) sets how many story missions the
goal needs, and `goal_challenges`
(0-168, default 25) how many challenge missions on top. With `final_mission_goal` (on by default) The Future of Hyrule
has no unlock item: it opens once you have the other clears, and clearing it wins. `goal_difficulty` makes the goal's
clears count only on that difficulty or a harder one (a harder clear counts for every easier difficulty).
`difficulty_lock` goes further: no clear below that difficulty counts for anything, and the client raises the game's
difficulty setting to at least that level whenever you are on the map.
`goal_hope_of_all_hyrule` adds The Hope of All Hyrule (every region's map at 100%) to the goal: a very long run. With `final_mission_goal`, clear The Future of Hyrule first (some of the map opens only after it); the goal is done once both are. Not available in `challenges_only`.

## Game modes

`game_mode` changes the shape of the run. Both alternatives open every service from the start and put every check
on level clears, spread evenly (bonus checks sent with each clear); recipes are items.
- **Story Only:** every check is on story missions (the Guardian of Remembrance missions too with the DLC). Each
  clear opens one new random story mission; with `mission_unlocks: items` (the default) story missions open by
  their unlock items instead, as in Standard. The goal is `goal_story_missions` clears. Korok seed and chest checks
  are the story missions' own (122 seeds, 153 chests, plus the Expansion Pass story's 28 chests).
- **Challenges Only:** every check is on challenge missions; story missions (except the pre-cleared Battle of
  Hyrule Field) and map quests don't appear. Each clear opens 3-8 more challenges; with
  `challenge_unlock_order: items` each challenge opens by its own unlock item instead, and 12 start unlocked. The goal
  is `goal_challenges` clears (0 = 50). Korok seed checks are the 12 seeds inside challenges; chest checks are only
  the Expansion Pass story's 28 chests (with the DLC those missions are challenges here).

## Pacing and DeathLink

There are no traps. With `steady_rewards` (on by default) story mission clears never hold your own filler.
`hero_level_cap` keeps heroes at 99 (they still level up and refill). With `death_link` on, your hero's HP reaching 0
in a mission is sent to the others, and a death from someone else defeats you at once: your health drops to 0 and the
game's normal defeat menu comes up (Restart Battle / Exit Scenario). Deaths that arrive while you're not in a mission are
ignored, and one that arrives while the game is paused lands when you unpause. (This needs the client's game mod from
0.9.91; with an older copy still installed your health stays at 0 until the next hit instead. Close the emulator once
and the client updates it.)

## Side content

With `challenge_unlock_order` and `quest_unlock_order` randomized (default), a random handful of challenges and
quests is open from the start and every completion (story clear, challenge or quest) opens 2-4 more. The client opens
and closes them in game and shows "Now open: ..." over the emulator window. Set either to vanilla to keep the game's
own order. `challenge_unlock_order: items` (off by default) makes every challenge open with its own
"Unlock: <challenge>" item instead, like story missions with `mission_unlocks: items`; it needs challenge checks.
Maz Koshia's trial and the fairy fountain challenges still wait for their quests. When another player
releases or collects, quests whose checks are already gone are completed for you (with their reward when the client
knows it). `region_hope_checks` makes each region's 100% "Hope" quest a check.

## Korok seeds, chests and progress checks

`korok_checks` and `chest_checks` (on by default) make every Korok seed ("Korok Seed: <mission> #n") and treasure chest
("Treasure Chest: <mission> #n") a check, sent the moment you find it. Seeds and chests that need a rune (Stasis
targets, bombable rocks, half-buried chests) expect that rune first.

Off by default ("Progress Checks" group):
- `hero_level_checks`: a check per hero every `hero_level_check_interval` levels up to `hero_level_check_max`
  ("Hero Level: Link Lv 20"). Higher levels expect more of the story first.
- `weapon_level_checks`: a check per hero when their best weapon reaches every `weapon_level_check_interval` levels
  up to `weapon_level_check_max` ("Weapon Level: Link Lv 10"). The game caps weapons at 20, 25 after A Monumental
  Undertaking and 30 after The Legendary Blacksmith; levels above a cap need its quest (or are left out).
- `enemy_defeat_checks`: enough of an enemy type defeated, counted by the trophies earned in total ("Defeated: Lynel
  (1)"). `material_checks`: enough of a material gathered in total ("Gathered: Hyrule Herb (2)"). Up to
  `gathering_check_tiers` rising counts each, scaled by `enemy_defeat_scale` / `material_scale` (percent). The client
  keeps the totals from the moment the seed first connects: spending doesn't lower them, and materials the client
  hands you don't count. Type `/gathered` (or use the Options tab) to see your totals and the next count each needs.
  A material held at the game's 999 limit gains nothing until some is spent.

## Sheikah Slate runes

`sheikah_runes` (default `shuffled`): all four runes from the start (`start_with_all`), `shuffled` (each rune is an item, Remote
Bombs too) or `vanilla` (from the story: Remote Bombs and Cryonis in The Battle of Hyrule Field, Magnesis and Stasis in
Road to the Ancient Lab).
The unmodded game hands runes out whenever those story missions count as cleared, so the client installs a small game
patch (the "AoC Archipelago" mod for game version 1.4.1, which also does the frame rates below) into Eden's and Ryujinx's mod folders while the emulator is
closed. With it, the game shows exactly the runes the client gives. Start the client before the game.

## Elemental rods and apples

`rod_items` (default on): the Fire Rod, Ice Rod and Lightning Rod are items. A rod whose item hasn't been found has no
slot in the item palette (hold L) at all, and one picked up in a mission is taken away again. The palette is set up when
a mission loads, so a rod found mid-mission appears from the next mission on. The lab's
"An Apple a Day" research (fire rod kills) expects the Fire Rod first. Off: the rods work as in the normal game.

`apple_items` (default off): healing apples are an item ("Apples"). Until it is found the apple slot (hold L, then B)
has no slot in the palette, and the apple count stays at 0 in missions as a fail-safe. Like the rods, it appears
from the next mission after the item arrives.

## Frame rate

`frame_rate` (default `off`, the game's own 30 left alone; the higher modes are experimental): `fps_60`, `fps_120` or `unlimited` let the game draw up to that many frames a second
in gameplay (cutscenes, menus and the world map stay at the game's own 30). An older YAML's `fps_30` means `off`. The game normally slows down when it can't draw its target frame rate; the client keeps it at real-time
speed whatever your PC draws, by choosing how many of the game's 1/60 s steps each drawn frame takes. How many frames
you get depends on your PC and emulator settings (resolution scale and GPU accuracy cost the most).
In the client, the Options tab or `/fps 60`, `/fps 120`, `/fps unlimited`, `/fps off` or `/fps seed` change it for your game;
`/fps` shows it. Remove other 60 FPS cheats for the game: they fight the client.

## Rules of the story

Story missions start with your own heroes in their party (`story_party: free`); a hero you don't have yet is never
forced in. With `story_party: borrowed` missions keep their own forced heroes, and any you
don't have are lent to you for that mission only (while the map cursor is on it and during the battle). Calamity Strikes needs Mipha, Daruk, Revali and Urbosa (the game traps any Champion you don't have after
it). Only challenges that restrict the party in the base game (for example "Daruk's Training") need the matching hero.

`mission_order` can shuffle which mission sits in each story slot. `side_missions_per_unlock` makes each
later slot also require completed challenges and quests (slot N needs N x that many).

## Known limitations

- EX Alerts stay playable but never hold checks (except Forgotten Temple): the game gives each one a monster when it
  appears, which the client can't set yet.
- Windows only; Ryujinx (Memory Manager Mode Software) or Eden (CPU accuracy Unsafe or Auto; recommended); both tested in full play.
- Universal Tracker works with this world without your YAML.

tutorials.text:
# Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity Randomizer Setup Guide

## What you need

- [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases/latest) 0.6.7 or newer
- `hyrule_warriors_aoc.apworld`, installed into Archipelago
- Your own legally dumped copy of the game, updated to v1.4.1, in **Eden** (recommended) or **Ryujinx** on Windows
- Ryujinx: Options > Settings > System > **Memory Manager Mode: Software**. Eden: **CPU accuracy Unsafe** (faster) or Auto.
  The client reads and writes the game's memory through these.

## 1. Make your YAML
Install the apworld (double-click it, or put it in `custom_worlds`). Open the Options Creator in the Archipelago
Launcher, or edit the sample YAML. Then generate as in the
[Archipelago Setup Guide](/tutorial/Archipelago/setup_en#generating-a-game).

## 2. Before the first session
Start the game once in your emulator so a save exists (if you have never played, pick New Game, wait for the first
cutscene, then close the game). Open only one emulator at a time.

## 3. Play
With the game **closed**, open **Age of Calamity Client** from the Archipelago Launcher and connect to your room
with your slot name. The client sets up this seed's save by itself: a new seed gets a starter save (your previous save
is kept and comes back when you connect to its seed again; switching between seeds works the same way). Then start
Age of Calamity and pick **Continue** (the client redraws the world map by itself whenever something opens; if an icon is ever missing, pause and go back to the map once).
The game reads its save only when it boots, so connect the client before starting the game. Everything else is
automatic:

- The client finds the running game by itself and says `Connected to Age of Calamity in Ryujinx` (or `in Eden`).
- Story missions, challenges, quests and weapons you complete or find are sent the moment the game registers them.
- Everything you receive is applied in game while you play: heroes become playable (and heroes you don't have are
  locked), upgrades, quest rewards, runes, mission unlocks, weapons, rupees, materials and XP.
- The world map follows the seed: only missions and challenges your seed has opened can be started.
- If the game isn't running, consumables you receive are written into the save file instead (backups in
  `%USERPROFILE%\AoC_Archipelago\backups`); everything else is applied the next time the game runs.
- Starting a New Game is detected, and everything you received is given again.
- The same seed can be played in both emulators: start the game once in the other one, close it, and type
  `/sync_saves`. From then on the newest save is copied over the older one whenever no game runs (with a backup).
- The client finds Ryujinx's data in `%APPDATA%\Ryujinx` and next to a portable Ryujinx, and Eden's in
  `%APPDATA%\eden` (a portable Eden while it runs). If your Ryujinx or Eden keeps its data elsewhere, use **Pick emulator folder…** in the Options tab (or `/emulator_folder <folder>`).

Useful commands (information only, nothing needs to be typed to play): `/check_hook` shows the game connection,
`/todo` your goal progress and what you can play now, `/inventory` what you have received, `/deliver` what is still waiting for the game,
`/saves` which save belongs to which seed, `/sync_saves` copies your save to the other emulator now.

Universal Tracker works with this world without your YAML.

## Troubleshooting
- **Game not detected:** load a save (not just the title screen). Ryujinx: Memory Manager Mode "Software". Eden: CPU
  accuracy Auto. The game must be v1.4.1. Close any other Age of Calamity client window and any second emulator.
- **No save found:** start the game once in your emulator; with a portable or moved Ryujinx or Eden use **Pick emulator folder…** (Options tab) or `/emulator_folder`.
- **Something went wrong:** quit without saving, or restore your save backup.
- **Version warning on connect:** the seed was made with an older apworld. New client features work with it; options
  added later only apply to newly generated seeds.

readme.text:
HYRULE WARRIORS: AGE OF CALAMITY - ARCHIPELAGO RANDOMIZER
=========================================================

Going forward, development focuses on the Eden emulator: new features are built and tested on Eden first. The new Royal Ancient Lab features in 0.9.81 have been tested on Eden only.

An Archipelago (https://archipelago.gg) multiworld randomizer for Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity, played on
the Ryujinx or Eden emulator on Windows. A live client runs beside the game and does everything automatically: it sends
your checks, gives you the items your friends find, locks and unlocks heroes, missions, challenges and quests, and
shows short notices over the game window.

DOWNLOAD THE APWORLD (latest version):
  https://github.com/DrPuffball/aoc-archipelago/releases/latest/download/hyrule_warriors_aoc.apworld

Latest version, ready to install (double-click it). All versions and notes: https://github.com/DrPuffball/aoc-archipelago/releases.

Testing release. The game is huge and there is a lot of ground to cover. Please report anything odd (see
REPORTING PROBLEMS below).

WHAT YOU NEED
-------------

- Computer: Windows (the client reads and writes the emulator's memory; Linux/macOS are not supported)
- Emulator: Eden (tested 0.2.1; recommended, actively updated and faster) or Ryujinx (tested 1.3.3), set up with your own keys and firmware dumped from your
  own Switch. The client detects which one you use; open only one at a time. No emulator, keys, firmware or game
  files are provided or linked here.
- Game: Your own legally dumped Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity (Switch, title ID 01002B00111A2000) updated to v1.4.1. The Expansion Pass (both waves) is used by default; without it, set include_dlc: false. This project contains no game files.
- Archipelago: 0.6.7 or newer (download: https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases/latest)
- This world: hyrule_warriors_aoc.apworld (direct download: https://github.com/DrPuffball/aoc-archipelago/releases/latest/download/hyrule_warriors_aoc.apworld)

INSTALLATION (ONCE)
-------------------

1. Install Archipelago.
2. Download hyrule_warriors_aoc.apworld
   (https://github.com/DrPuffball/aoc-archipelago/releases/latest/download/hyrule_warriors_aoc.apworld)
   and double-click it (or copy it into Archipelago's custom_worlds folder,
   usually C:\ProgramData\Archipelago\custom_worlds). Restart the Archipelago Launcher.
3. Emulator setting. Ryujinx: Options > Settings > System > Memory Manager Mode: Software, then save (the client
   can't read the game without it). Eden: CPU accuracy Unsafe (about 10% faster in battle) or Auto; not
   Accurate or Paranoid.
4. Make sure the game is updated to v1.4.1 in your emulator.
5. Nothing to install in the emulator: the client puts the "AoC Archipelago" game mod into Eden and Ryujinx by
   itself whenever no emulator is running (start the client before the game) and keeps it up to date. Leave it on in
   the game's Add-Ons list, and remove any other 60 FPS cheat or mod for the game.
6. Start the game once in your emulator so a save exists (if you never played: New Game, wait for the first
   cutscene, close the game).

MAKING YOUR OPTIONS
-------------------

Archipelago Launcher > Options Creator > Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity, or edit the sample
Hyrule Warriors Age of Calamity.yaml (change name:). Give the YAML to whoever generates the multiworld; they need
this apworld installed too. The defaults are the tested setup; the options most people change:

- starting_character_count: random heroes you start with (default 4).
- challenge_checks / quest_checks / lab_checks / weapon_checks / korok_checks / chest_checks: what holds checks
  (default: challenges, quests, the Royal Ancient Lab, Korok seeds and treasure chests on, weapons off).
- Progress checks (all off by default): hero_level_checks, weapon_level_checks (a check every few levels),
  enemy_defeat_checks and material_checks (defeat or gather enough in total), with gathering_check_tiers and scales.
- rod_items (on): the Fire, Ice and Lightning Rod are items; a rod's slot stays hidden until you find it.
  apple_items (off): healing apples are an item too.
- challenge_unlock_order / quest_unlock_order: randomized (default) or vanilla.
- mission_unlocks: items (default) = each story mission opens with its own item from the multiworld (you start
  with 2); story_order = in order.
- first_mission: which missions you can start on (default any story mission; random_early = chapters 1-2).
- goal_story_missions / goal_challenges / goal_quests / goal_all_heroes: what the goal needs (default 20 of the 28
  story missions and 25 challenges). With final_mission_goal (on), The Future of Hyrule opens once you have them and clearing it wins.
- game_mode: standard, story_only (every check on story missions, each clear opens the next) or challenges_only
  (every check on challenges, no story or map quests).
- difficulty_checks / difficulty_lock: extra checks for harder clears, or clears below a difficulty don't count.
- Open from the Start: Sheikah Sensor, stables, shops and dye shop open from the start (on); trackers pre-done (off).
- hint_mission_unlocks / hint_heroes: free hints; hero_level_cap: heroes stay at 99 (level-ups still refill you).
- filler_weights: filler mix (default about 40% material bundles in three sizes).
- sheikah_runes: shuffled (default; all four runes, Remote Bombs included, are items) | start_with_all | vanilla.
- frame_rate (experimental): off (default, the game's own 30) | fps_60 | fps_120 | unlimited. Above 30 the game
  stays at real speed however many frames your PC manages. Change it any time in the client's Options tab or with /fps.
- death_link: share deaths with the other players. A received death defeats your hero at once (the game's normal
  defeat menu, Restart Battle works).

GENERATING AND HOSTING A ROOM (the host does this once per run)
---------------------------------------------------------------

The archipelago.gg website can't generate games for custom worlds like this one, so the host generates locally:

1. Install this apworld (see above) and put every player's YAML into Archipelago's "Players" folder
   (usually C:\ProgramData\Archipelago\Players).
2. Archipelago Launcher > Generate. The finished game appears as a .zip in Archipelago's "output" folder.
3. Host it: upload that .zip at https://archipelago.gg/uploads (free, gives you a room address to share),
   or Archipelago Launcher > Host to run the server on your own PC.
4. Every player connects the Age of Calamity Client to that room address with their slot name.

PLAYING
-------

1. Keep the game closed. Archipelago Launcher > Age of Calamity Client > connect to the room (address, e.g.
   archipelago.gg:38281, and your slot name).
2. For a new seed the client installs a starter save by itself ("Starter save installed"): the game's forced
   opening is skipped, and you start on the world map with your random starting heroes and the seed's opening
   missions. The Battle of Hyrule Field is shuffled into the story like any other mission (pre-cleared in
   challenges_only). Your previous save is kept (see below).
3. Start Age of Calamity in Ryujinx or Eden and pick Continue. The client finds the game by itself.
4. Play normally. Notices appear in the emulator window: items sent and received, what a gift went to, and - when you
   highlight a mission, challenge or quest on the world map - what its checks hold. When an item opens something, the
   world map redraws by itself.

Switching emulators: the client keeps a seed's save the same in Ryujinx and Eden. Start the game once in the other
emulator, close it, and type /sync_saves; after that, whenever no game runs, the newest save is copied over the
older one (with a backup; never a New Game over progress).

Switching between seeds: each save belongs to the room it was played in. Close the game and connect to another
room: the client swaps the saves (yours are kept in %USERPROFILE%\AoC_Archipelago\saves) and gives each room its own
save back. It never replaces a save while the game runs, nor a save with progress it can't place
(/starter_save does that on purpose, keeping a copy).

The client window's Options tab has a button or switch for every command, grouped by what it's for (frame rate,
display, your progress, saves, troubleshooting); hover one to see what it does. Typed commands work too: /todo (goal
progress, what to play), /inventory, /gathered, /check_hook, /deliver, /saves, /sync_saves, /emulator_folder,
/starter_save, /goal_banner, /deathlink (on/off any time), /research, /fps (frame-rate mode), /accept_save. Full details: SETUP_GUIDE.md.

Save safety: if the first read after connecting shows many clears the server has never seen, or would finish your
goal at once (another seed's save in the slot), the client holds them back. Type /accept_save only if the save really
is this seed's.

HOW THE RANDOMIZER WORKS
------------------------

- Checks: clearing story missions, challenges and quests, Korok seeds ("Korok Seed: <mission> #n") and treasure
  chests ("Treasure Chest: <mission> #n"), sent the moment you pick them up (weapon pickups and progress checks
  optional). When there are more items than
  checks, extra "bonus" checks are spread evenly over the missions you can play before the goal.
- Items: heroes, per-hero upgrades (hearts, combo moves, special gauge, abilities), quest rewards, mission unlock
  items, the four Sheikah Slate runes (with sheikah_runes: shuffled), the three rods (rod_items), and filler (hero XP gifts, weapon bundles, rupees, material bundles,
  meals). Most quest-reward items give their reward directly (recipes, Sheikah Sensor, rune and stat upgrades,
  discounts, Smithy upgrades, lessons, dyes, research, Expansion Pass abilities and royal gifts). Buying the quest only
  sends its check. Maz Koshia's trials are the exception: each trial is the next fight, so its item opens the quest.
- Royal Ancient Lab (with lab_checks): the lab is on the map from the start and all 35 nodes are open. Each node you buy
  sends a check. It still needs its materials and its own condition, such as 100 Remote Bomb kills. The two relic nodes
  need The Future of Hyrule, so with final_mission_goal they hold no checks. Most rewards are items.
- Side content opens at random by default: a few challenges and quests are open from the start and every completion
  opens 2-4 more (post-story ones included). Either kind can be set to the game's own order instead.
- Story safety: Calamity Strikes needs Mipha, Daruk, Revali and Urbosa (the game traps any Champion you don't have
  after it). Other story missions, including Water and Fire and Air and Lightning, follow the seed's order.
- Heroes you don't have are locked (never during a battle); story missions put your own heroes in their forced party
  slots.
- When another player releases or collects, quests whose checks are gone are completed for you (with their reward
  where the client knows it).

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
-----------------

- Windows only, game v1.4.1 only. Ryujinx needs Memory Manager Mode Software; Eden needs CPU accuracy Unsafe or Auto. Both are
  tested in full play (Eden 0.2.1: a whole session of missions, quests, items, DLC and save switching).
- Shuffled runes, rods, instant DeathLink and the higher frame rates need the game mod (the client installs it).
- Frame rates above 30 are experimental: cutscenes and the world map stay at 30, and the pause menu does
  too unless you switch it on in the Options tab. Flurry rushes can feel a little off. Frames depend on your PC (the emulated
  CPU is the usual limit). In Eden keep "Fast CPU time" off: it makes the game run fast.
- A rod or apple found mid-mission shows in your item palette from the next mission on.
- The Expansion Pass is on by default (include_dlc): the Guardian of Remembrance missions are story missions, EX
  challenges and quests hold checks, and Purah & Robbie, Sooga and the Battle-Tested Guardian are items. EX Alerts
  stay playable but never hold checks (except Forgotten Temple). Without the DLC in your emulator, the client
  takes the DLC out of the goal and sends its checks, so the seed stays winnable; or set include_dlc: false.
- Post-story missions started before the story ends are untested: report any that won't load or behave oddly.
- The world map has twice got stuck in its "new icons appear" sequence (under investigation): returning to the title
  screen usually helps; save often.
- Three lab nodes keep the game's own reward (Roll Out the Research, The Technology of Disassembly, Sensor of the Heart).
- Universal Tracker works without your YAML: connect it to your slot and it rebuilds the seed from the server.

REPORTING PROBLEMS
------------------

First see TROUBLESHOOTING.md (the usual fixes: close the game before switching seeds, start the client
before the emulator so it can install the game mod, /todo for what the goal needs).

Open an issue: https://github.com/DrPuffball/aoc-archipelago/issues with: what happened and what you expected, your YAML, the client log (Archipelago's
logs folder, newest Launcher_*.txt).
Testers can also type /research on in the client: it then records which of its changes the game kept
or undid, quest rewards, and the client's last actions if the game crashes, in
%USERPROFILE%\AoC_Archipelago\research\findings.jsonl; attach that file too.

SOURCE
------

hyrule_warriors_aoc/ is the world (logic, items, options), its client (client/) and tests (test/).
REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md explains how the game keeps its state and how the client reads and changes it (for anyone,
human or AI, picking up the project).

# Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity for Archipelago - 0.9.92 (testing release)

An Archipelago world plus a live client for Age of Calamity (v1.4.1) on Ryujinx or Eden (Windows). Setup: see
`SETUP_GUIDE.md`. Having trouble? See `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Full change history: `RELEASE_NOTES.md` in the zip.

## What's new

- **Korok seeds and treasure chests are checks** (on by default): 134 seeds and 153 story chests (+28 with the
  Expansion Pass), sent the moment you pick them up.
- **Progress checks** (off by default): hero levels, weapon levels, enemies defeated and materials gathered.
- **Rods as items** (on by default): the Fire, Ice and Lightning Rod stay hidden until you find them. Apples can be an
  item too (`apple_items`, off by default).
- **The Battle of Hyrule Field is shuffled into the story** like any other mission.
- **Instant DeathLink:** a received death defeats your hero at once, with the game's normal defeat menu.
  DeathLink can now be switched on or off in the client (`/deathlink` or the Options tab).
- **The world map redraws by itself** when something opens: no more pausing to see new missions.
- **New Options tab in the client:** every command as a button or switch, grouped by purpose, with hover help.
- **Frame rates (experimental):** map cursor, minimap ping and menu animations keep their speed at any frame rate;
  the pause menu can follow it too (Options tab). In-engine cutscenes, special attacks and a mission's
  last seconds stay at the game's own 30. **Frame rates above 30 are still experimental:** if anything misbehaves,
  set the frame rate back to the game's own 30 (the default) and report it.
- **Eden is now the recommended emulator** (actively updated, and faster): set its CPU accuracy to Unsafe for about
  10% more frames in battle.

New seeds are needed for the new checks and items; seeds made with 0.9.89 keep working. Please update, then restart
the client.
